description: I joined this challenge with a friend, we will try to train a small AI model and combine it with some hardware I have at home
summary: On missions to the Moon and Mars, radio delays to Earth reach up to 40 minutes round-trip, meaning astronauts cannot wait for Earth doctors during a medical emergency. We built BiometrAR, an offline Edge AI health monitor running on a bare ESP32 microcontroller. Trained on real ISS radiation data from NASA's RadLab API and NASA HRP clinical limits, it analyzes 10 vitals in under 1 millisecond and hosts a simple, offline Wi-Fi web dashboard (http://192.168.4.1) with instant treatment instructions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
BiometrAR is an offline AI health monitor that diagnoses astronaut emergencies in under 1 millisecond. A Python script (train_local.py) fetches real ISS radiation data from the NASA RadLab API, trains a neural network on 10 vitals using NASA HRP and CSA thresholds, and exports the model to pure C++ (model_weights.h). Flashed onto a bare ESP32, it hosts an offline Wi-Fi webpage (http://192.168.4.1) with a color-coded astronaut figure, 4 simple vitals cards, and clear treatment steps.

Impact & Why It Matters
Mars-to-Earth radio delays take up to 40 minutes. Aegis-EVA gives astronauts instant, easy-to-read medical decisions on a \$5 microcontroller with zero internet or wiring—and can also be used for offline emergency triage in remote areas on Earth.

Tools & Hardware Used

•Hardware: Bare ESP32-WROOM (Wi-Fi hotspot, GPIO 0 button, GPIO 2 LED).

•Code: Python (scikit-learn, NumPy, Pandas), Arduino C++ (WiFi.h, WebServer.h), HTML/CSS/JS.

•SI Disclosure: AI coding tools assisted in writing the training script, C++ exporter, and ESP32 web server.
